chunk.text: HRP Ongoing HRP Research in Space Human Investigations on NASA's Artemis II Mission ARCHeR A study on Artemis II monitored astronauts' well-being, activity, and sleep patterns to learn more about human health and performance in deep space. Read About ARCHeR Immune Biomarkers Scientists analyzed blood and saliva samples from Artemis II crew members to see how deep space changes the immune system. Read About Immune Biomarkers Artemis II Standard Measures Crews supplied a consistent set of health information to a data bank so that future researchers can learn more about astronaut health. Read About Artemis II Standard Measures Human Investigations in Low Earth Orbit B-Complex Investigating if a daily B vitamin supplement can prevent or mitigate brain and eye changes that may affect some humans in space Read About B-Complex Brain Fluid Pressure Examining the relationship between fluid pressure inside the skull and changes to the eyes and brain of astronauts Read About Brain Fluid Pressure CIPHER Providing a better understand of how the human body changes while orbiting the Earth via a suite of studies examining multiple body systems Read About CIPHER Simulating Manual Piloting for Moon Landings Assessing how gravity transitions may affect the piloting capabilities of astronauts for future Moon landings Read About Simulating Manual Piloting for Moon Landings Spacecraft Occupant Protection Surveying crew members' potential discomfort during re-entry to Earth and combining it with sensor data on spacecraft Read About Spacecraft Occupant Protection Spinal Fluid Biomarkers Detecting
